text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Bahraini press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Bahrain launches drive to cut alarming road accidents, which killed 17 people in the last two months.
- Bahraini Crown Prince Sheikh Hamad is likely to visit Qatar. Bahrain and Qatar are locked in a territorial dispute over small islands in the Gulf.
- Gulf Petrochemical Industries Company posts $52 million operating profit in 1996. It made $90 million operating profit in 1995.
- Transport minister says Bahrain, Kuwait, Qatar and the United Arab Emirates have agreed to construct an $80 million deep sea cable to link their communication networks.
- Gulf Arab states hail improved relations between Bahrain and Qatar. Doha welcomes agreement to open embassies in each other's capital.

- Bahrain's State Security Court continues to try 59 suspects accused of plotting to topple the government. Around 81 suspects had been accused but only 59 had been arrested. the rest are still at large.
- Big activity on the Bahrain Stock Exchange. More than three million shares were traded on the bourse on Wednesday.
